utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Sorry. I do apologise for -- to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was the corridor closed before the civilian authorities found out about this information or afterwards? Can you pinpoint this in terms of time?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I'm tired now, and I cannot exactly say.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, you personally and the civilian authorities - I mean, the Crisis Staff and the War Presidency and later, of course, the Municipal Assembly of Samac - did you address the competent military authorities with a view to preventing crime among the military? Did you inform them about this? Did you make efforts to have this resolved? I'm talking about the period when you held the civilian positions.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, both in writing and orally.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to tender into evidence a document which is actually notice -- notice signed by the person in charge for the forest company with regard to some -- some criminal incidents. For the benefit of my learned friend, that's RH36.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have a look at this document and we're going to comment on it a bit. Did you have any contact with this document previously? Do you know what this is about?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I understand that this document was created on the 30th of January, 1993, by the company called PIK Samac and that somebody signed it on behalf of director Stevan Tutnjevic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What is this document about?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: This is unplanned and unrelenting cutting of woods in the municipality of Samac and in the war zone, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Is there any mention as to how the members of the military units behaved?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. They behaved aggressively. They did not allow the workers of the agricultural company to enter their estate, and this is a reaction on the part of the leadership of the agricultural company towards everybody regarding the unplanned cutting of trees.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And who was this letter addressed to?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: President of the executive board of the municipality of Samac, president of the municipality of Samac, head of the Department of Economy of the municipality of Samac, the Chief of Defence department of the municipality of Samac, the head of the Public Security Station, the military police, and their archives.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If there is no objection, Your Honour, I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No objection, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Can we have the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It will be D61/1 and D61/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Dr. Simic, during your term of office as president of the municipal assembly and before that, did you report to some other authorities on crime -- the occurrence of crime?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... The number of this -- of next documents is RB10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, you asked a question though, and Dr. Simic didn't have the opportunity to answer before you introduced the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's just my --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Take a look at the document, Dr. Simic, see what this is, and then we are going to discuss it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may ask for one thing on behalf of our client. I've been informed by them that they are -- when they look at the ELMO, they just see English version of the document. And I believe that there are enough versions in English for the Trial Chamber. So for their benefit, it would be better to place a B/C/S version of the document on the ELMO so they could understand what it's all about.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note that they do not have copies of the documents that Defence counsel present, so it is indispensable for them to have copies, either on the ELMO or in the booths. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, you've heard what the interpreters have said.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Vis-a-vis the suggestion by Mr. Lazarevic. So make an effort to give copies to the interpreters in the booths.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I see that it is number 16/93, but there is no date. If I am right, if I am -- if we look at this number, when I say that this was sometime around the beginning of 1993 --

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What is this document about?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, if Your Honours please, at this point --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If there's some magic in the number 16/93 that enables us to ascertain that the letter was sent in early -- early 1993, as Mr. Pantelic suggested to the witness, then perhaps we ought to know what it is that indicates why it is that 16/93 must mean early 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So bearing in mind this number "16," and bearing in mind the number of documents that were there during the sessions of the municipal assembly, during their work, what can you conclude? Of course, we cannot say precisely whether this 16 document was in April, May, or September, but what do you infer when you say that it's the beginning of 1993?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Only one assembly had 1 to 30 items on the agenda, so this is a small number, a number 16. And obviously, this is the beginning of 1993 because later on this number was much bigger.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Further on your personal recollection with regard to this letter, what can you do with it in terms of time?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: This is when the Muslim and Croat armies were trying to cut off that corridor. And every day they were launching operations. This is about 4 or 5 kilometres away as the crow flies -- or rather, it is 4 or 5 kilometres as the crow flies that they tried to cut off, and they wanted to leave the Serbs without any possibility of communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. I'm just asking you about time. I'm interested in the time. 1993, at which time in 1993? Just that. Do you have any personal recollections regarding this? I assume that you signed this document.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: This is the winter of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, please tell us, did you discuss anything at parliament or in commissions with regard to the phenomenon that you refer to in this letter, and what happened after this letter?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: This phenomenon was discussed as the municipal parliament because this was a problem in practically all local communes. The problem was in the following: Wherever the army was stationed, it left some damage. There was looting, there was theft, and there was no end to this. And every day brigades came and went. They changed their locations. They changed their command posts, operative zones, and quite simply during the war this was a constant problem, how to secure personal and social property.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you get any response from the military authorities regarding the prevention of crime, lootings, and theft?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I received some response orally, as far as I can remember, some promises that the military police in cooperation with the civilian police will reinforce its activities aimed at preventing any kind of crime in the territory of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If there is no objection, could we have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have the numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It will be D62/1 and D62/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And one more question regarding this period of time: You've mentioned this before, but perhaps you could give us some additional information. What was the work of the Serb Assembly of the Municipality of Samac like in 1992, towards the end? Did it function then?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, it functioned throughout the time; however, it has had regular sessions, since late 1992. And up until this day, its sessions are usually held once a month or once every two months.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When you spoke about difficulties at the medical centre and problems relating to procuring sufficient equipment and supplies for haemodialysis, I have an article here and I would like you to give your comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... R30.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you remember this article in the papers?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Does it speak about the difficulties the medical centre in Samac faced and the dialysis department?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If we take a look at the second page, do you see there any statements given by non-Serb residents of Samac?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please just read out the names mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Munira Zaimovic, Ferida Arslanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What is their ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: They're Muslims. Danica Pacak is a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have the exhibit number for this, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No objection, I take it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it will be D63/1 and D63/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the meantime, I have a couple of copies for the interpreters' unit. If you can pass these documents to them in order to help them. On the top right-hand side, there is an internal number that we are using here so that they can immediately localise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to discuss with you the activity of the Crisis Staff directed at securing everything that was necessary for the agriculture. Were there such efforts made by the Crisis Staff and executive organs?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, those were regular activities of a municipal assembly which every year would adopt the plan for harvesting and then there would be implemented through the executive organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Then I would like to know whether the War Presidency also was involved in certain problems with utilities, infrastructure, and tried to repair houses that were damaged by war activities so that residents could live in them.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes. The War Presidency was involved in this; however, it was always transferred to the executive organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... RH10. And then I would like to have certain ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No objection, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Can we have the documents and the numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be D64/1 and D64/1 ter, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When was this decision adopted, the one before you now?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: On the 6th of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you sign it?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What is this decision about? What was the objective, the intention of the War Presidency when this conclusion was adopted?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: The objective was to establish a public construction company that would repair all buildings that had been destroyed due to war operations in the territory of the entire municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did this pertain to the entire population regardless of their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, to the entire population and the entire municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Usher. You can take these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday we spoke about certain activities of the HDZ in the region.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Let me ask for clarification. This document, the second paragraph, it says, "We hereby instruct the executive committee." Is this the executive committee of the War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's the executive committee of the municipality but of Serbian Municipality of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That is my understanding, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday we spoke about what you knew about certain activities of the HDZ in Bosanska Posavina, and now I would like you to take a look at this document and give us your comments if you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: For the Defence, it's R7.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dr. Simic, do you know Ivan Brizic, who signed this document? Have you heard of him?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Is the content of your document in conformity with what you know about the intentions of the Croat people in Bosanska Posavina region?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes. I heard these stories and allegations from Mate Nujic and another person who was a member of the Croat community in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If there is no objection, I would like to tender this document into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Sorry, would Your Honours just bear with me for a moment, please. Thank you. Thank you. If Your Honours please, no objection to the introduction of this particular document. I wonder if Mr. Pantelic, who has up until fairly recently been giving extra copies to us at the time the document is introduced - in addition to the binder that he's already provided - will be providing us with further documents in court, as you were up until just recently?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have the number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it will be D65/1 and D65/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Dr. Simic, do you know who Iko Stanic is?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell us something about this gentleman. Who is he? What is his occupation?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I had information that he was from Derventa and that he was president of the Croat Community of Bosanska Posavina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I would like to discuss with the witness document -- our internal number is R3.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As we can see, this document hasn't been signed. It bears no stamp. It is what it is. The Defence was unable to obtain another document apart from this one. Now, please tell us what you know about the intentions and objectives of the Croat Community of Bosanska Posavina and the territorial scope of that community basically are in conformity with what is said here in this document.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Mostly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us when was this document drafted? What is the date in the upper left corner?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I believe it is the 12th of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you have any objections, Mr. Di Fazio?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I would like to have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, can we have the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it will be D66/1 and D66/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now, Dr. Simic, I have another document of the War Presidency which is not of a particular relevance. It's a technical document. However, it is important because of some topics that I want to bring up.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: For the Defence, it's RH24. In fact, this is the decision to appoint the secretary of the -- secretariat of Economic Affairs on a municipal level.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suppose, and you can correct me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: The document you handed over to us a moment ago dated the 12th of November, 1991, and signed by Iko Stanic, what do you intend to show by this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the basis of the testimony of my client here with regard to the establishment of Croatian Community of Bosnian Posavina and especially with regard to the municipalities which should be according to that plan should be included in this region, where you can find also under the number 4, Bosanski Samac, it's just corroborative evidence to the context in which certain events in Samac and in the region were -- were cured at that time in 1991 and 1992, since the period and time frame of the document is from October 1991 until the end of 1993. So it's just a context. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's go back to this document. I suppose that this is -- have you looked at it? You can see the heading and the stamp and all that. You can see that it is a certain decision of the War Presidency, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So please tell me, when was this decision taken, the one that you have in front of you?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: The 1st of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were you present at the War Presidency session then?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Who signed this decision?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You can -- if there is no objections, I would like to have -- to an exhibit number for this document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No, there is no objection. But perhaps if I might adopt Judge Lindholm's question, what is the relevance of it? That's a threshold that a document has to overcome before it's admissible. It's got to be relevant. And apart from any other considerations -- and I don't want the stand in the way of the Defence in producing documents if they're important to their case. I don't want to do that at all. But for the life of me, I just can't understand the significance of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because it seems the -- even the accused says he wasn't the president then, he doesn't know who signed, so what is the relevance --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And what can the accused say about this?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. I will gladly explain that. First of all, since this document was issued on the 1st of August, 1992, when my client was on the medical treatment, and since we have one of the documents issued by a War Presidency for Mr. Stevan Todorovic, if you remember, to travel on the session of republican parliament of Republika Srpska, which was signed by the secretary of the War Presidency, and since we are a layperson with regard to the handwriting analysis, probably I will make certain comparisons and then expert will say whether the document issued to Mr. Stevan Todorovic at that time, at the end of July 1992, and this particular document, which was issued on the 1st of August, bears actually same signature. So in -- in that way it might be relevant. And also it will show the way how certain documents in certain institutions were signed. Whether it was strictly assigned to certain person in his authority or in practice during the war operations and during that time practically the other persons might be in a situation to sign, on behalf of one institution, certain documents. But that's the issue for the closing argument, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Let's have the numbers, then.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be D67/1 and D67/1 ter, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] The same applies to the next document we would like to produce. This is RH13. This is also a sort of decision to relieve the secretary of Secretariat for Economic Affairs, also issued on the 1st of August. So it's the second document which might be of importance for the topics that I just raised.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So my question is the same as with regard to the previous document. We can agree that this document was adopted on the 1st of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, by the War Presidency. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were you present at that session?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And later on when you returned, did they inform you that these documents had been passed?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: By and large, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If there is no objection, I would like to tender this document into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to discuss a payroll list of the War Presidency of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have the number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It will be D68/1 and D68/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Now I would like to discuss a document. It's a -- it's a payroll list for War Presidency. RH18 is our internal number. It's a payroll list for the month of July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dr. Simic, we've already talked about the contents of these payrolls, so there are no special questions here. All I want you to do is to confirm for me if this is the payroll for July 1992.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And on behalf of the War Presidency of the Municipality of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If there's no objections, I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No objection, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have the numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be D69/1 and D69/1 ter, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I have another document. It's a pay list for the month of November 1992, also for War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. So, Dr. Simic, is this --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry. RH16.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Is this the payroll for November 1992?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, for some members of the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And what about others?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to the decree, the president, the vice-president, and councilmen, who I suppose were on the payroll in other places.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When you say "councilmen," you mean the councilmen in the municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If there is no objection, I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: There is no objection to the document being given its -- being tendered into evidence, if Your Honours please. But again, it's a question of making things clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: To the Chamber. From the answers of the witness -- I gather from -- if you read the exchange between Mr. Pantelic and the witness, that this document that we're just producing now contains only some of the War Presidency members, because other War Presidency members were being paid via their positions in the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So these -- I take it that this salary list is not exhaustive of -- of all the War Presidency members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And if that's the case that's common to all of these salaries, then we'd better -- we'd better know that, had we not? Because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The composition of the War Presidency is matter of importance and it may affect --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- Crisis Staff salary records as well. I raised this issue yesterday, I believe, when I think the first payroll was introduced. And I asked specifically if it was an exhaustive, complete list of the Crisis Staff, because I think it related to Crisis Staff documents, and the answer was that it did. As the documents have come in, therefore, I've been under the impression that -- and the Chamber may be under the same impression that I am, is that these payroll lists show you the membership, and they may not. And that's what I'm concerned about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Let's have the explanation from the accused on the matters raised by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We introduced yesterday the payroll of the Crisis Staff, and that was the final payroll list. That was followed by the decree of the president of the republic saying that the Crisis Staff were being disbanded and War Presidencies introduced instead, and indeed informing members of the War Presidency. And it said that the president and the vice-president of the municipal assembly - and that was their decree that was tendered - then the president and vice-president of the executive council and some councilmen from amongst the councilmen or in the municipal assembly. So specifically here we had Mr. Milan Babic, who was a councilmen and subsequently president of the municipality of Pelagicevo, because at that time already the municipality of Pelagicevo was about to split away. So who is missing here is the president and vice-president of the executive council who were on the payroll of the executive council, and Milan Babic who was on the payroll of the municipality of Pelagicevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. We'll proceed. Yes. Can we have the numbers first, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It's D70/1 and D70/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Something -- something because of the interpretation, something is not indicated in the answer you gave us and which we have in the transcript, so could you please repeat it for us. You mentioned that the Prosecutor had tendered this decree in this case. Will you please provide us with this information.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the Prosecution's exhibit -- I may be wrong, but I don't think I am -- the Prosecution tendered the decree on the establishment of War Presidencies, and that decree - can we get this document - specifies who were members of the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This, Dr. Simic, was merely --

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: In contrast with the Crisis Staff, which was -- which was in its final shape according to that payroll.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I asked you merely because of the transcript, because your words were not faithfully put here when you said it, so that is why I had to ask you. And as for the analysis of this document and all the rest, now this is a legal matter and we shall come to that later on. We shall discuss it when time comes for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, thank you, Your Honour. I think it's about time for the break. In the next part, I will just go through certain exhibits on the Prosecution list, certain decisions of the Crisis Staff and War Presidency. Then my plan is to go through certain issues raised by Mr. Stevan Todorovic as well of some of the other Prosecutor witnesses, which I think that it will be a fairly brief process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So you're expecting to wind up today?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, as it's not quite 1.00, might Mr. Re take this opportunity to produce some documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We have --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- that arise from the document the other day of the experts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. Might I tender into evidence material arising from the cross-examination of Professor Nikolic and Dr. Kecmanovic. I tender the Badinter report opinions, that's the conference on Yugoslavia arbitration committee's opinions 1, 2, 3, and 4 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please speak up or come closer to the microphone. The interpreters can barely hear him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Excuse me for just a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, how many documents do you have?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I have four Badinter reports, three --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It will take a bit of time, won't they? We have to understand that the accused requires a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And other matter, if you allow me, Your Honour: We -- frankly, we were not in the situation - especially Defence for Mr. Simic, Dr. Simic - were not able to physically check all these documents. So I kindly ask a few days for us during the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: To be able to look at them. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So we can resolve that and then we will inform the Trial Chamber accordingly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We shall adjourn for lunch and we will resume our proceedings at 14.30 hours. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.01 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber has been informed that the Prosecution wish to raise a procedural matter before we continue with examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's quite correct, Your Honour. Before we continue, the Prosecution has a matter which it must raise and place on the record before the Trial Chamber concerning Rule 68 and disclosure under the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. It has come to the Prosecution's attention today that it is not in a position to confidently say that it has provided all material which may be exculpatory under Rule 68 to the three accused. I raise the matter now after Mr. Simic has -- Dr. Simic has started giving his evidence because it may affect the evidence or the defence which he may be running in his case. The Prosecution can say that it did an all-system search of all the material it has in its collection in 1998. The search has to be updated and it has to be updated properly to pick up all possible exculpatory material. It has then to be reviewed by Prosecution lawyers before material can be turned over to the Defence. The Prosecution has -- one moment. During the course of the trial, the Prosecution has disclosed material in relation to each of the witnesses that it called and is confident that that material has produced everything under Rule 68. The Prosecution has also done searches, name searches of the three accused, the three present accused. One of them is ready; that's Dr. Blagoje Simic. It has produced some seven volumes. We got it over the last day or couple of days. The Prosecution has not yet had a chance to review the material, to assess it, to translate -- draft translate any material there, and to turn over anything potentially exculpatory to the accused Dr. Simic before he completes his examination-in-chief. The remaining two searches on the other two accused, I'm informed today as of lunchtime, will be available by close of business Tuesday. The all-systems search, which is across all of the Prosecution's some-3 million document, searching for all relevant search criteria in this case which may impact upon the Defence of the accused and may potentially - we don't know - produce exculpatory material, I'm told as of lunchtime today, will take 100 personnel person days to complete. The acting Prosecutor has made a decision to put a team on to this straight away to try and accomplish this task as soon as possible, but with past experience and the pressure on the OTP's information support unit system, it could take several months to complete the all-system search of everything relevant in this particular case. We have discussed this. We had a meeting with the Defence counsel; it came to our attention today. We brought this to the attention of the Defence counsel immediately at lunchtime. The search has to be done and it has to be done properly. We have copies of the search criteria which we are providing to Defence counsel as to the search which was done before. We will, with Defence counsel's assistance -- we discussed this with them over lunch -- put in any term which is they consider to be relevant to their Defence, thus maybe producing more material, potentially relevant material. So the Prosecution at this point can only say we have -- we don't know whether there is additional material there. There may be; there may not be. The impact on the case at the moment as we see it is that in paragraphs 11 and 12 of the indictment, the three accused charged jointly in relation to a common purpose, it would appear that -- I can say that at the moment this is -- it's hypothetical as to what may well be produced. We just don't know. But we are extremely anxious to ensure that this is done properly and the trial does not proceed in a way -- in any way which would be unfair to the three accused. The Prosecution also say that when the original searches were done, the Prosecution did not know what the potential defence was going to be, so the original search criteria was obviously different to what it would be today at the close of the Prosecution case and the beginning of the Defence case. And we add it's only been since, I think, November last year that an all-system search could have been possible, and there have been extreme pressures on the Prosecution searching system, especially with the Milosevic trial in recent times. It would appear that there are several alternatives available as to what we can do in this situation: The Defence have indicated they would seek an adjournment to seek instructions as to where they go from here. And at this stage I raise the matter so that the Defence and Trial Chamber are aware that at this stage, at least, we cannot confidently say that we've provided everything under Rule 68.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, there's just one further matter that I wish to add to that. Mr. Re omitted to mention that the process hasn't been static. It didn't come to a halt. It's been ongoing. I know for a fact that the former Prosecutor in this matter, Ms. Paterson, was engaged in disclosure, the exercise of disclosure of Rule 68 material to the Defence. She was engaged in that when I first arrived, and that was the beginning of 2001. And of course that procedure was ongoing last year with Ms. Reidy tending to disclosure and searching for any exculpatory material throughout her period of time here at the OTP, as indeed were Mr. Weiner and myself. So the situation is nowhere near as alarming as you may think at first. It's really the -- this last search that Mr. Re mentioned that is of -- of crucial interest, the ultimate search, the all-system search, and of course the searches for the -- other searches for the individual defendants that he mentioned. But I just wanted to stress that it's been ongoing and continuous whilst the matter was in the hands of Ms. Paterson and also last year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And this is on an indictment which has been with the Prosecution since 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, I don't know the precise date of the indictment, but I believe it goes back to the mid-1990s, if Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And if the search has been ongoing, why hasn't the Trial Chamber been informed, especially at the close of the Prosecution case, why wasn't the Trial Chamber informed that you are not yet -- you have not yet completed Rule 86 obligation -- Rule 68 obligations? Because there was no notice to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I was under the impression that the searches had been properly conducted and complete. This --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. Because the submission has been --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Sorry, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Properly conducted and ongoing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It started about November last year.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That the search system started about November last year.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. Well, perhaps Mr. Re can address you on that. I don't know what this all-system search is and when it came into evening. Mr. Lay might be able to answer you on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Might I be able to confer with my colleagues. I might be able to answer your inquiry more precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There are two different types of searches we're talk about here. As Mr. Di Fazio correctly addressed you on, Your Honours, the searches he was referring to are witness searches. They are witness-specific searches relating to the witnesses who gave evidence in this case. The trial team did searches of particular indexes which the Prosecution has to search for exculpatory material and handed that over on an ongoing basis to the Defence teams. That relates to the witnesses who were called in this case. It was an all-systems search as well. There were two searches done. The search I'm talking about is an all-systems search of the entire Prosecution collections, and there's a number of collections which have been added since 1998 which haven't been searched, and those are the ones which will pick up things other than just the defendants' names. It's a search of all varying criteria of keyword which may come up in the case, like "4th Detachment," the "Cafe AS," or whatever. There's a lot of different things which may turn up in different indexes which have not been systematically searched; that's the difference. Of course material was handed over on an ongoing basis during the trial. That is why the Prosecution cannot confidently say that it has uncovered and reviewed all potentially exculpatory material on an all-system search. Does that assist, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. As a result of what the Prosecution have said, the Trial Chamber's decision is that we'll go ahead with the examination-in-chief of Blagoje Simic, up to the questions that Mr. Pantelic had prepared. We shall not close the examination-in-chief, and then we will hear the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, if I may address the Court. Unlike for the Prosecution, it is very alarming issue for the Defence. I will just give you one example --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I haven't yet given you an opportunity to answer. I simply said just wind up your questions. You won't close the examination-in-chief and then the Defence -- because all the three are affected. Then the Defence will put whatever points they want to put on record and then the Trial Chamber will consider that before we proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour. But I don't know in which part I can cut my examination-in-chief, because the line of questioning might be related to the issue that it was just raised with the Prosecution. If there is something of importance for the Defence, then maybe I will not follow certain line of questioning. So I'm a little bit confused now how I can fulfil my obligation as Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no. The point is you started yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So just complete it as you prepared it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And then whatever -- whatever documents the Prosecution are talking about are given to you, you'll be able to address the Chamber. So -- with the other three accused. Because the point is the -- what the Prosecution have raised may have far-reaching effects than we can immediately see right now. Yes. So the Trial Chamber doesn't want to stop the proceedings. Complete your questions. The examination-in-chief will not be closed, and thereafter all the Defence counsels will be able to address the Chamber on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I understand, Your Honour. But I have another problem: First of all, I need at least half an hour to discuss this new issue with my client, and then we need at least 15 minutes just to consult among the Defence, because it may affect the Defence case and also the trial by itself, because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, Mr. Pantelic. I don't think you understand what I'm saying. You are not going to close your case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I understand that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you get instructions from the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Complete your examination-in-chief. We won't close it. And then we'll deal with this issue. Because it affects the whole Defence case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And in particular this examination-in-chief also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Anyway, just go ahead and complete the questions you had prepared and then we'll deal with this matter. Yes. I have to explain to the accused person that the Trial Chamber has taken note of what the Prosecution have said. Of course the accused person may not understand it completely. Time will be given to the counsel and all the accused persons to be able to resolve this matter in the best way possible. All the Trial Chamber is trying to do is just complete the questioning that you had prepared.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I would like to discuss with Dr. Simic some of the Prosecutor's exhibits already tendered into the evidence. Could I have the assistance of Mr. Usher and the registrar. It is Exhibit P25.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dr. Simic, a few questions regarding this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me. I think we have the same problem as before. For Mr. Tadic and Mr. Zaric, we should have the B/C/S version on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think that would be the best solution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Doctor, could you put the Serbian version on the ELMO and then you can see it either there on the ELMO or on the screen in front of you. Please tell me, please, who drafted the text of this decision?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: The executive council of the Municipal Assembly of Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What was the objective of this decision?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: The objective was to fund the erection of a monument to fallen soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were there any specific criteria set as to who and under what conditions can use money from this fund?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, it is set out in this decision. I can't comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And this financial assistance, did it apply to the families of fallen soldiers solely from Samac municipality or any other one as well?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: It applied to all the soldiers who were killed while serving in the Army of Republika Srpska, regardless of where they were from.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. I've finished with this exhibit. Now I would like to discuss Exhibit P49. Please put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Is this a form that was used in the Crisis Staff by the Crisis Staff for these purposes?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Is this your signature here?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: It isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know that on behalf of the Crisis Staff the Zastava 101 vehicle was temporarily confiscated from Delic Dragan, who was its owner?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was this confiscation of a vehicle ever discussed at the Crisis Staff sessions?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: How was it discussed?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: It was said that all kinds of requisitions which take place during the war are the sole responsibility of the Ministry of Defence and that nobody else was authorised to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were there any cases of abuse in these matters where certain individuals carried out requisitions without the knowledge of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, I believe that this is one of such cases of abuse, although I cannot confirm that this document is authentic. However, soon thereafter this stamp was put out of use and a new stamp was introduced. And once the Crisis Staff ceased to exist, then this stamp wasn't valid any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, just a matter of lack of clarity in the evidence again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: A question was asked if this particular confiscation was discussed at the Crisis Staff, and the witness said yes, it was. Mr. Pantelic asked how was it discussed. And then the witness said that all kinds of requisitions which took place during the war were the responsibility of the Ministry of Defence. I understood his answer to mean that this particular requisition, the one mentioned in P49, was discussed. Now, if so, Mr. Pantelic should follow that up and make it clear for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. You have understood what the Prosecution is talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Dr. Simic, was this particular case of requisition of a vehicle, of Zastava 101 owned by Dragan Delic, was this particular requisition order discussed at the Crisis Staff session?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: This particular order was not discussed at the Crisis Staff session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Usher. Now I would like to discuss the Exhibit P71.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, I have a supplemental question to that of the one just posed by Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Because -- on page 72, line 15 Dr. Simic says, "Well, I believe that this is one of such cases of abuse," which from a logical grammatical construction seems to refer back to this document in question, to this particular requisition. So this is a little bit unclear, what we have here on the record at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. I'll clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we established here that you did not sign this order. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We have also established that this order was not discussed at the Crisis Staff session.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That this phenomenon of requisition was discussed at the Crisis Staff sessions in general terms.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And that it had been concluded that this fell under the responsibility of the municipal department of the Ministry of Defence, that they were in charge of these matters in wartime.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: It was concluded that it was solely within the scope of responsibilities of the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And that you knew that there were individual cases of abuse of the institution of the Crisis Staff and its stamp.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes. However, all such cases had to be reviewed by the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. P71, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you ever seen this decision?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Here at the Tribunal within the materials presented here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were decisions of the Crisis Staff typed by such a typewriter with this kind of letters?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What alphabet was used?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Cyrillic alphabet, whereas this is a Latin one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you ever discuss this document with Stevan Todorovic and this phenomenon described in this document, namely, the isolation of Croats?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: No, I never discussed this document with Stevan Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Have you ever met with Stevan Todorovic in the premises of my office in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: How many times have you met with me before you surrendered to the Tribunal, The Hague Tribunal? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Two or three times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me. Mr. Pantelic --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Could you explain perhaps what the relevance of your question is to has Dr. Simic met with Stevan Todorovic in the premises of your office in Belgrade. What does it mean? What relevance does it have?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yeah, because Mr. Todorovic said before this Trial Chamber that on one occasion he discussed that matter and that specific document with Dr. Simic in my office, so it's a question of clarification of the evidence that was produced here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Thank you for refreshing my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And my last question: In mid-May in 1992, were members of Croat nation, citizens of Croat ethnicity in Bosanski Samac, placed in vital facilities in town?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me again, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Again for the sake of clarification, what do you mean when you say "placed in vital facilities in town"?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Would you have in mind under the term "vital facilities," and I don't mean pertaining to this decision. But generally, what do you have in mind under that term?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Waterworks, hospital, police [as interpreted], power supply company --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- silos.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have to object to the transcript. I have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I haven't heard that Mr. Simic said "police," and I see that it is in transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will clarify that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Since there is a problem with the transcript, you didn't say "police;" however, that's recorded here. On the other hand, you did say "silo," and that wasn't recorded here. So let's repeat it again. What do you understand by "vital facilities in town"?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Waterworks or the central building of the water supply company, electric power supply company, and by this I mean transmission station, silo, hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now it's clear in the transcript. Could we have Exhibit P72, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you can see this, this is a decision on establishing War Presidencies in municipalities during -- when there is an immediate threat of war or an emergency, dated 8th of June. And let us now take a look at Article 2 and establish whether the answer that you gave us this morning had to do with this.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: The War Presidency consists of the republic deputy, and as a rule president of the municipal assembly or his deputy, or rather, vice-president, president of the executive council or his deputy, or vice-president or a citizen who is an assemblyman. This is what I meant when I said today that the membership of the War Presidency is regulated by this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have Exhibit P73, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please tell me what was the objective of this decision.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did the War Presidency -- although, you've already answered this -- but tell us, please, was -- pursuant to this decree, was the War Presidency or its composition changed in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Is this your signature down here?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know perhaps whose signature it is?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Usher. Please, P74.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you remember this decision?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What was the motive for passing this decision?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: An improvement in nutrition of soldiers and an appeal to the command of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Is this unit, special battalion, which is mentioned in this decision, did it exist within the brigade?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If you know, please tell us how many soldiers were there in this special battalion and who were these soldiers.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. There were several hundred soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Where were these soldiers from?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: From the territory of Samac municipality as well as Pelagicevo and Srpsko Orasje municipalities and Odzak.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So that means those were local residents, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes. To a degree, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were there non-Serbs there as well? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I believe that there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. P75, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you recall this document?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you sign it?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Most probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And who prepared the text of the document?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: The executive council of the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And what was the purpose behind this letter?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Economic linkage, economic ties between the two municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. P76, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you recall this document?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And what was the purpose, or rather, the objective and the backdrop against which this document was passed?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: To allow the executive council to draw the money from the budget and buy identical uniforms for the strike battalion at the request of the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Is that that same battalion of several hundred men, locals from the area?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Usher. Please, P77.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: From this Tribunal's records.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did the Crisis Staff take this order?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Is there a signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: There isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What type of letters do we have in this document?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: These are Latin characters.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Have you perhaps heard during the past period who could have been -- who could be the author of this document? Do you have any information?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I can only make guesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And what would your suggestion be?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Witness Stevan Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... P78.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: No, until I saw the records of this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And have you seen any documents with a seal like this one, earlier in your work?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And is it the institution indicated on the stamp, SAO Semberija and Majevica?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. Could we have now P81, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before we make comments about this document, SAO north of Bosnia, as you told us yesterday, was never in working order. It never really came to be.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, that's so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And at approximately what time did the municipality -- the Serb municipality of Bosanski Samac join SAO Semberija and Majevica?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: In the early days of combat operations in Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Will you please cast a look at the document. Have you seen it before?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Who prepared it?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: The executive council.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: The executive council of the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And what was the purpose behind this disposition?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Milos Bogdanovic's proposal to recruit somebody from the municipality into this service. So the Ministry of Defence's proposal to recruit somebody, to bring something into this service.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was that in conformity with law, to pass such a disposition on behalf of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And how long did this disposition last?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Seven days -- three to seven days.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: How many did you say?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Three to seven days.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I'm -- and I say this knowing that I can clarify matters myself in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: But the sooner clarified, the better, I submit. I'm not entirely sure what Mr. Pantelic -- what the witness means by the use of the word "disposition." And if it means the appointment of Simo Zaric -- sorry, if somebody brought -- yes. There's a reference to this disposition lasting seven -- three to seven days. We should surely have some idea or understanding what caused the end of this disposition, whatever disposition might be. It's just not clear to me. And when you come to read the transcript, you might wonder what precisely it means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think the witness can explain that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because the administrative agencies [Realtime transcript read in error word "agent"] concluded that this paper was not in conformity with law. It was sent back for redrafting, and we withdrew it and stopped it. That is, we declared it invalid. We vacated it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is that clear, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It's clearer, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Once again, please, will you repeat your answer because in the transcript in English it says "agents," and that -- could then be associated with police services. But you said "administration," so will you please repeat your answer once again.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Administrative [Realtime transcript read in error word "admonitive"] agencies compared it with the existing laws and decided that this document was not in conformity with law. So they returned it for redrafting and the Crisis Staff decided to vacate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic, again on the same note for clarity, I take it on line 15 of the transcript, what I think I heard in the translation was Dr. Simic said "administrative agencies." We have "admonitive agent" at the moment. Administrative agencies. Is that the right word?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I think that -- that was the issue for the court recorder. So probably in -- but I am very grateful for your intervention, Your Honour. Of course. Thank you. Now, could we have P88, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you familiar with this order?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And who issued it?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: The executive council.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When you read it, is there anything illegal in it? Is there anything wrongful with it? And what is its purpose? And please pay attention in particular and comment on item 3, if you can. Specifically, was the purpose of this order to engage in plunder or to prevent plunder?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: The purpose of this order was to prevent plunder.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Is this your signature here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic. This is just a question now of the type style. I thought we heard a few minutes ago that the Cyrillic alphabet was used and not the Latin alphabet in documents produced post-April 1992. Now, here, if my eyes don't deceive me, we have the Latin alphabet.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: So could you explain how come -- or rather, Dr. Simic explain how come this document is using the Latin alphabet.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Because, Your Honour, I must draw your attention on page 86, line 6, where the author -- actually the institution of this document was mentioned. That is the executive board or the executive council. So that was my understanding, but I will clarify that if you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: No, I understand that was the case. But -- so the executive board used the Latin alphabet, whereas the Crisis Staff used the Cyrillic alphabet. Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will ask the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you remember, first, did the technical services draft and type these documents by and large?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And again by and large, did the executive council use prevalently Cyrillic or Latin, and what about the Crisis Staff, and what about some other agencies, if, that is, you have any knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: We did not have enough Cyrillic typewriters, so those that existed were used by the Crisis Staff in the early days, because the earlier state did not have Cyrillic typewriters in the administrative agency. They were all Latin alphabet. And this, I think, is a computer printout. And so the Latin alphabet was used for a while until they also managed to procure Cyrillic typewriters.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My next question: So you in the Crisis Staff did not discuss this order, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Let me preface my remark with again, I know it's a matter I can go to in cross-examination. But you're hearing evidence from the witness now and now is a good time for him to make his evidence clear. This is said to be an executive council document -- executive board -- executive council document, not a Crisis Staff document. We're looking at P88.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. It says -- unless I'm looking at the wrong document. I don't understand. It says "Crisis Staff," at the bottom, "Crisis Staff" at the top," nothing on it about the executive board. I just wanted to make sure I was looking at the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: ERN number 00 --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. I am looking at the right document. I'm not mistaken. Perhaps a question might be asked as to what is it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You are saying that it shows "Crisis Staff" at the top and "Crisis Staff" at the --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It shows "Crisis Staff" from top to bottom, all over. If there's something that the witness knows that he can tell us that makes this an executive board document, then he should explain it to the Judges, because that's the evidence. He says it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Doctor -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Dr. Simic, can you explain that, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, these are the very early days of the war, when there is a lot of confusion in everything. So there was confusion in the authorities as well, and later on it was defined and we were physically separated several kilometres, I mean, the executive from the legislative powers, from the executive power. And every order that followed was increasingly precise, saying the executive council, the executive council, and one knows what is are the decisions of the Crisis Staff. And every decision of the Crisis Staff should also bear my signature; that was common knowledge. But these are the very early days and there was -- the very early days of the war and there was a lot of confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And you say that practically this was done by the executive council by using the name of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have P89, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please give me your comments regarding this document, whether this kind of decision was adopted at the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Who prepared the text of this decision?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: The executive council.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What was the objective of this decision?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Introducing a state of emergency in the territory of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: For what reasons?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: These are legal matters now, and I think it is all written here. It is hard for me to comment on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
