utterances.text: All right. Was Samac bombed by the Croat forces at that time?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were there incursions by sabotage groups of the enemy army?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were there problems with electricity, water, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Usher. Please, P90. In the meantime, Your Honour, what is our timing for today? In 4.15 or --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: 16.15. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you aware of this decision?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What was the basis for passing this decision?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: The proposal of the Ministry of Defence, or rather, of the executive council. And the primary objective was to prevent desertion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did a higher institution -- I mean, higher than the Municipality of Samac -- pass a similar decision?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: The SAO Semberija and Majevica did too, but have soon this was dealt with by the Ministry of the Interior and the Ministry of Defence. Therefore, this soon became invalid, because republic enactments always supersede municipal ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But at that time were you duty-bound to respect the decisions of the SAO Semberija and Majevica?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was the Crisis Staff ever in charge of issuing passes to the civilian population for leaving the territory of the municipality of Samac?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Who was in charge of that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Passes were issued -- well, it depended on who they were for. Soldiers from a brigade, civilians, the Ministry of Defence, or civilians in the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. Could we have P91.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you aware of this order?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the period of war operations the party SDS, did it carry out its activities?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: On the basis of what?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: On the basis of the decree of the government of Republika Srpska, that in times of imminent threat of war and in a state of war the activity of political parties shall be frozen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please, P92.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you aware of this decision?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The meeting of the municipal parliament, can you remember in terms of the date when this decision was passed when did the municipal parliament meet approximately?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Looking at the date of this decision --

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- can you say after that date when was there a session of the municipal parliament?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: The next month in 1992, that is to say, December 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And this decision bears which date?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: The 28th of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What was the basic objective of this decision?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: These premises were used by the Serb Democratic Party before the war too; however, during the war the military entered this entire building, particularly upstairs. There were many heavy weapons that were brought up there because this was at the immediate front line. And when fire was exchanged, this building was being destroyed day after day. In this way, we didn't want the military to use it for war operations. We wanted a bunker to be built in front of this building so that the building would not be totally destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Is that building on the banks of the Sava River?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: As the crow flies, how far away is the line where the enemy army was?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: 100 to 150 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. Please, P93.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you aware of this decision?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What was the objective of passing this decision?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: It is self-explanatory. The objective was to prevent the selling of alcoholic beverages.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were there any incidents caused by alcohol at that time in Samac?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Almost every day there were incidents as a consequence of war operations and also as a consequence of the extensive use of alcohol. Also, there was alcohol that was of dubious quality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was this directly related to the uncontrolled use of weapons as well?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Inter alia that, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did this threaten the safety of the civilian population of Samac?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. P94, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is this your signature on the document?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of this document?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you comment on this document? Is this a certificate stating that plunder can be carried out, or is the reason for this certificate quite different? What is your understanding of this document?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I think that the document is self-explanatory, that there are family ties involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do I understand this correctly, that this Simo Stojcevic from Pelagicevo can go to the house of Andjelko Ljubic and take things -- Andjelko Ljubic's things, because that is actually the home of Simo Stojcevic's parents. So that is private property.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: That is what this document says.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. Please, P95.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you aware of this decision?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What was the objective of passing this decision?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: For humanitarian aid to be centralised and equally distributed among the local commune, because it would happen that certain local communes would have continuous aid and others did not receive any aid whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Who prepared this draft decision, the draft of this decision?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: The executive council.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I am asking you whether it was the staff of the executive council or the executive council itself.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: The staff, the professional staff of the executive council, but under the control of the executive council.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. Please could we have Exhibit P96.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you aware of this document?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What was the point of this document?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: This document -- or rather, there is this same kind of document that says "Slavko Nikolic." This is his son or his relative. Slavko Nikolic lived in Samac, but originally he came from Serbia. He was a member of the Crisis Staff of the town of Samac. So he felt the need and he thought he could, because he originally came from Serbia, ensure or provide some humanitarian aid.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Slavoljub Nikolic and Vidoje Nikolic, were they ever involved in -- in the organisation that supplied Samac with weapons?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were they involved in the organised sending of trained personnel so that they would join the units of the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Usher. Please, P97.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assume this is the document that you referred to, but in order to avoid any misunderstanding, you just said that he was a member of the Crisis Staff of the town of Samac. Could you please explain what that means in relation to the municipality.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, the town of Samac is a local commune. Every local commune at that time had a Crisis Staff of its own.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And what were the powers of these local Crisis Staffs, so to speak?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Always related to the community itself, to public utilities, to what related to the work of their assemblies and the executive councils of their assemblies.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You mean of the local communes?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You said that, and it was not in the transcript, so I would like it to be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. P98, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you aware of this document?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Are we going to 4.15 today? Do you want to break now and discuss that matter in relation to -- let the Defence counsel speak to their clients now about that problem. Would it be better to break now as opposed to breaking at 4.15 when the day is over, since he's going to continue on with this witness anyway into tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber is of the view that we'll break now, and we'll continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And Your Honour, do I understand well that we can confer with our clients now here at the premises of the Tribunal? That's my understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before they are taken to the Detention Unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Because the closing time at UN is quarter to 5.00, so technically it will not be possible to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Since the matter was raised rather abruptly, yes, you'll be allowed to confer with your clients. And yes, since it's examination-in-chief, so you're allowed to contact your client. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Limited to the issue -- the procedural issue that is we raised. We are not discussing any --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, that was raised by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Court will adjourn until tomorrow morning at 9.30 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
